comment: The reviewed state of upstream CoreProtect. See transformer/src/main/java/net/deltik/mc/libreprotect/transformer/Audit.java for the rules.
The build fails on a FAIL finding unless 'allow' lists that rule at that site. A REVIEW finding blocks releases until a maintainer accepts it.
A site ending in '*' matches by prefix. Pin FAIL-rule allowances to a method so new uses get reviewed; REVIEW-rule allowances can cover a whole class so upstream renames don't cause churn.

lines: the reviewed state of each upstream line that LibreProtect builds: 'release', the release that upstream.lock pins, and 'development', upstream's default branch, which development builds track. Each is what the audit observed in the build of its line that a maintainer last accepted, and its 'upstream' names that build: the ref and commit built, and 'jarSha256', the SHA-256 of upstream's JAR. The audit accepts what any line has, so a build of one line needs no review for what the other line has too. To accept upstream changes, review what changed (scripts/lp review), then run scripts/lp accept, which replaces the build's line with what it observed (dist/audit-observed.json), and commit the result. A line that LibreProtect no longer builds, such as v24.1 once a CoreProtect 25 release is locked, can be kept under another name while the extensions keep its ways.

jarSha256: the extensions' unit tests expect exactly the ways of the upstream JARs that the lines name, and skip those tests on any other upstream JAR, whose audit reports any change to the capabilities instead. So accepting a build whose ways changed means updating those tests too, as scripts/lp accept says. The audit doesn't check it, so a new upstream never needs a review for it.

egressExemptPrefixes: com/clickhouse/ is the ClickHouse JDBC driver, bundled on upstream's master branch after v24.1. It connects only to the ClickHouse server configured in config.yml, so its network code is neither redirected nor failed by the audit. Its bundled org/roaringbitmap/ and org/jspecify/annotations/ are accepted with it.

The dynamic-class-loading allowances for VersionUtils, BlockMetaCodec and EntityDataCodec are only for upstream's master branch after v24.1 (CoreProtect 25), as are, in the development line, org.duckdb:duckdb_jdbc, which CoreProtect compiles against and plugin.yml's libraries has the server download when it loads the plugin, outside LibreProtect's network policy, and com.mysql:mysql-connector-j for upstream's own tests.

capabilities: how LibreProtect's extensions work with the upstream JAR, from the capability report that their build writes and the JAR bundles as META-INF/libreprotect/capabilities.tsv. 'capability <id>' is the way they take (or 'absent' where upstream lacks the feature, 'unavailable' where they can't use it). Under the capability and way that use them, 'code <id>/<way> <method>' is a fingerprint of an upstream method whose behavior the way relies on beyond its signature, including the code of its nest that it runs without dispatch: its private, static and final methods and constructors, the methods of its final classes, and those that the compiler wrote, 'doc <id>/<way> <path>' a hash of upstream documentation it follows, 'enum <id>/<way> <class>' the constants of an upstream enum it names, and 'optional <id>/<way> <member>' whether upstream has a member it does without. An observed key=value that no line has is a capability-change REVIEW: check that the extensions still do the right thing with what changed, then accept it. A key that a build doesn't observe is no REVIEW, since another line may have it, except for a 'capability <id>' that the report no longer has. Since code, documents, enums and members are keyed by the way that relies on them, one line's code is never accepted under another line's way: an upstream that reverts a class but keeps its newer design still asks for a review.

versionReads: the upstream methods that read a plugin's version or full name (getVersion() or getFullName() of PluginDescriptionFile, getVersion() or getDisplayName() of PluginMeta) or name plugin.yml in a string, as code that reads it itself does; the same in both lines. CoreProtect compares its own version with others only in VersionUtils.getPluginVersion(), which the transformer has read upstream's version instead of LibreProtect's. StatusCommand, Patch and ShutdownService only show the version, loadWorldEdit reads WorldEdit's, and getBranch reads the branch from plugin.yml. A new method is a version-read REVIEW: if CoreProtect compares its own version there, it would compare LibreProtect's, whose leading numbers name upstream's nearest release tag, so extend the transformer before accepting it.

licenses: CoreProtect's own licensing, as key=value lines. 'file <path>' is the SHA-256 of each license-like file anywhere in upstream's source: a name with a word such as LICENSE, LICENSING, COPYING, NOTICE, EULA or TERMS at its start or after a separator, as in MIT-LICENSE or THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, or any file at any depth in a LICENSES directory (for a symbolic link, where it points and the SHA-256 of that file). 'pom licenses' is every field of each license that upstream's pom declares. 'header' is the SHA-256 of each distinct header of upstream's Java files: its comments before the package statement and among the imports, with the years of copyright notices replaced by #. Both lines have only the root LICENSE, the Artistic License 2.0, with no licenses in the pom and no Java file headers. scripts/lp sources archives upstream's files as the audit reads them, whatever upstream's .gitattributes says. Unlike the rest of the audit, a change here fails every build, development builds too, since LibreProtect may no longer be allowed to distribute the JAR or the source archive: an observed key=value that no line has fails, and so does an upstream without a LICENSE or COPYING file at its root. A key that a build doesn't observe needs nothing, since another line may have it. To accept a change, make sure that LibreProtect may still distribute CoreProtect under the GPL, as section 4(c)(ii) of the Artistic License 2.0 allows, then accept the build with scripts/lp accept --licenses. If CoreProtect is no longer under the Artistic License 2.0, also update what names it: NOTICE, LICENSES/, the License section of README.md, Differences.java, scripts/ci/publish.sh, scripts/ci/modrinth.sh and the README that scripts/lp sources writes.

allow.reason: Runs the constant command 'sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string' on macOS to read the CPU model for /co status. Local only.

Bundled HikariCP's JNDI lookup, only reached when a JNDI name is configured. CoreProtect never sets one.

Sets java.io.tmpdir to 'cache' for SQLite's native library extraction. Upstream behavior that affects the whole server, but not a network or privacy concern.
